_about: Hand-written catalog data for build_presets.py. Every description and equation here is our own text. Values come from the Ready pattern named in 'source'. See tools/README.md for the keys.

Gray–Scott.citation: P. Gray & S. K. Scott (1984) Chem. Eng. Sci. 39:1087; J. E. Pearson (1993) Science 261:189
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a - a b^2 + F\,(1 - a)
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a b^2 - (F + K)\, b

FitzHugh–Nagumo.citation: R. FitzHugh (1961) Biophys. J. 1:445; J. Nagumo, S. Arimoto & S. Yoshizawa (1962) Proc. IRE 50:2061; Hagberg & Meron (1994) Nonlinearity 7:805
equations: \partial_t a = k_1 a - k_2 a^2 - a^3 - b + \nabla^2 a
\partial_t b = \epsilon\,(k_3 a - a_1 b - a_0) + \delta\, \nabla^2 b

Ginzburg–Landau.citation: I. S. Aranson & L. Kramer (2002) Rev. Mod. Phys. 74:99
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \alpha a - \gamma b + (-\beta a + \delta b)(a^2 + b^2)
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + \alpha b + \gamma a + (-\beta b - \delta a)(a^2 + b^2)

Turing.citation: A. M. Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37
equations: \partial_t a = k\,(16 - a b) + D_a \nabla^2 a
\partial_t b = \max\big(-b,\; k\,(a b - b - 12) + D_b \nabla^2 b\big)

Yang (coupled Brusselators).citation: L. Yang, M. Dolnik, A. M. Zhabotinsky & I. R. Epstein (2002) Phys. Rev. Lett. 88:208303
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \alpha(c - a) + p_1 - (1 + p_2) a + a^2 b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + \alpha(d - b) + p_2 a - a^2 b
\partial_t c = D_c \nabla^2 c + \alpha(a - c) + p_1 - (1 + p_2) c + c^2 d
\partial_t d = D_d \nabla^2 d + \alpha(b - d) + p_2 c - c^2 d

Kytta (coupled Brusselators).citation: K. Kyttä (2007) MSc thesis, Helsinki University of Technology; L. Yang et al. (2002) Phys. Rev. Lett. 88:208303
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + q\,a c\,(c - a) + p_1 - (1 + p_2) a + a^2 b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + q\,b d\,(d - b) + p_2 a - a^2 b
\partial_t c = D_c \nabla^2 c + q\,a c\,(a - c) + p_1 - (1 + p_2) c + c^2 d
\partial_t d = D_d \nabla^2 d + q\,b d\,(b - d) + p_2 c - c^2 d

Swift–Hohenberg.citation: M. Pennybacker & A. C. Newell (2013) Phys. Rev. Lett. 110:248104; J. Swift & P. C. Hohenberg (1977) Phys. Rev. A 15:319
equations: \partial_t a = \mu a - (1 + \nabla^2)^2 a + \beta a^2 - a^3

Kuramoto–Sivashinsky.citation: Y. Kuramoto & T. Tsuzuki (1976) Prog. Theor. Phys. 55:356; G. I. Sivashinsky (1977) Acta Astronautica 4:1177
equations:
\partial_t a = w_4 
abla^4 a + w_2 
abla^2 a + w_g\, |
abla a|^2 + s\, a

Rosenzweig–MacArthur.citation: M. L. Rosenzweig & R. H. MacArthur (1963) Am. Nat. 97:209
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + a(1 - a) - \frac{a}{a + h}\, b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + k \frac{a}{a + h}\, b - m b

Morozov (plankton).citation: A. Morozov, S. Petrovskii & B.-L. Li (2008) J. Theor. Biol. 250:22

Heat and waves.citation: J. Fourier (1822) Théorie analytique de la chaleur

presets.name: Pearson θ: spots and stripes
presets.description: A small square of catalyst in a sea of fresh substrate. With K = 0.06 and F = 0.04 the front breaks into a slow mix of spots and short stripes that fills the whole torus.

presets.name: Mitosis
presets.description: Spots that grow, pinch in the middle and split in two, again and again, until they pack the plane. Same model and seed as Pearson θ, with F and K moved into the self-replicating region.

presets.name: Coral growth
presets.description: Branching fingers grow out from the seed and fold into a coral-like maze. The fingers never cross, so the finished pattern is one connected labyrinth.

presets.name: Chaotic waves
presets.description: At low feed rate the medium is excitable: pulses of catalyst run outward, collide, and break into turbulent, ever-changing wave fronts.

presets.name: U-Skate glider
presets.citation: R. P. Munafo (2014) U-Skate World, mrob.com/pub/comp/xmorphia; J. E. Pearson (1993) Science 261:189
presets.description: Near F = 0.062, K = 0.0609 the uniform state is almost stable and small structures keep their shape. Three blocks cut from the catalyst make a U-shaped glider that slides across the grid until it meets the wall.

presets.name: U-Skate rings
presets.citation: R. P. Munafo (2014) U-Skate World, mrob.com/pub/comp/xmorphia; J. E. Pearson (1993) Science 261:189
presets.description: In the same near-stable U-Skate regime, a ring and three holes cut into the catalyst. The ring slowly opens and the holes drift; the structures change shape only a little at a time.

presets.name: Self-replicating spots
presets.description: A noisy block of catalyst, with the substrate lowered by the same amount, breaks into spots. Each spot grows, divides, and the daughters push away from each other until spots fill the box.

presets.name: Noisy mitosis
presets.citation: A. Lesmes, D. Hochberg, F. Morán & J. Pérez-Mercader (2003) Phys. Rev. Lett. 91:238301
presets.description: Gray–Scott with a noise source. A third field c holds a pseudo-random value in [-1, 1] that the formula remixes every step and feeds into the substrate. Three seeds split into a few spots that jitter and drift instead of sitting still.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a - a b^2 + F(1 - a) + \sigma\, \xi
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a b^2 - (F + k) b
\xi \leftarrow (\xi + \nabla^2 \xi) \bmod 1

presets.name: Noise-driven spots
presets.citation: A. Lesmes, D. Hochberg, F. Morán & J. Pérez-Mercader (2003) Phys. Rev. Lett. 91:238301
presets.description: With these values the plain Gray–Scott spots would die. Added noise keeps the pattern alive: it grows from three seeds into a restless field of spots and fragments.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a - a b^2 + F(1 - a) + \sigma\, \xi
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a b^2 - (F + k) b
\xi \leftarrow (\xi + \nabla^2 \xi) \bmod 1

presets.name: Gray–Scott parameter map
presets.description: K grows from left to right and F grows along the vertical axis, so each part of the grid runs a different Gray–Scott system. Spots, stripes, mazes, waves and empty regions sit next to each other like Pearson's catalog.
equations: \partial_t a = 2D \nabla^2 a - a b^2 + F(y)\,(1 - a)
\partial_t b = D \nabla^2 b + a b^2 - (F(y) + k(x))\, b

presets.name: Stenciled feed rate
presets.description: A third field c works as a stencil: where c = 1 the kill rate is a little lower. Spots grow and divide only inside the stenciled letters-like blocks and stay out of the rest.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a - a b^2 + F(1 - a)
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a b^2 - (F + K - 0.005\,c)\, b
presets.citation: J. E. Pearson (1993) Science 261:189; parameter stencil idea from Ready (GollyGang)

presets.name: Froese: spots with waste
presets.citation: T. Froese, N. Virgo & T. Ikegami (2014) Artificial Life 20:55
presets.description: A Gray–Scott variant in which the catalyst leaves a waste product c that slows its own reaction. Spots move away from their own trails and leave dark tracks behind them.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a - e^{-w c} a b^2 + r(1 - a)
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + e^{-w c} a b^2 - k b
\partial_t c = k b - k_c c

presets.name: Brusselator
presets.citation: I. Prigogine & R. Lefever (1968) J. Chem. Phys. 48:1695
presets.description: The classic model of an autocatalytic chemical oscillator. With B above the Hopf threshold the random start turns into a field of oscillating, drifting patches and spiral fragments.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + k_1 A + k_2 a^2 b - k_3 B a - k_4 a
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b - k_2 a^2 b + k_3 B a

presets.name: Tip splitting
presets.description: Excited fronts grow into the resting medium. Each tip becomes unstable and splits in two, so the fronts branch again and again into a labyrinth.

presets.name: Ising fronts
presets.description: In this regime the medium has two stable states, like the up and down spins of an Ising magnet. A noisy vertical strip splits into a pair of fronts; the fronts slowly ripple and fold into a field of stripes.

presets.name: Pulsating spots
presets.description: A 2D slice of a 3D Ready pattern. Excited blobs grow, break, and pulse; the pieces become spots that breathe in and out.

presets.name: FitzHugh–Nagumo parameter map
presets.description: ε grows from left to right and the diffusion ratio δ grows along the vertical axis. One grid shows the stationary Turing spots and stripes, the travelling waves, and the uniform states of the model.
equations: \partial_t a = a - a^3 - b + D \nabla^2 a
\partial_t b = \epsilon(x)\,(a - a_1 b - a_0) + \delta(y)\, D \nabla^2 b

presets.name: Tip-splitting web
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Cornus Ammonis; FitzHugh–Nagumo after Hagberg & Meron (1994) Nonlinearity 7:805
presets.description: An experimental FitzHugh–Nagumo variant. A Sobel edge term couples the two fields along their gradients, and the splitting fronts weave into a fine web.
equations:
\partial_t a = s\,(
abla_S a \cdot 
abla_S b) + k_1 a - k_2 a^2 - a^3 - b + 
abla^2 a
\partial_t b = D_u (D_{us} \textstyle\sum_{8} a - a) + \epsilon(k_3 a - a_1 b - a_0) + \delta \nabla^2 b

presets.name: Complex Ginzburg–Landau
presets.description: The general equation for a field that oscillates near a Hopf bifurcation. Small noise grows into phase waves that organise around spiral defects. The view shows the real part.

presets.name: Ginzburg–Landau defects
presets.description: The same equation, but the view shows the amplitude |A| in a third field. Spiral cores show as dark points where the amplitude falls to zero.

presets.name: Ginzburg–Landau ramps
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Dan Wills; I. S. Aranson & L. Kramer (2002) Rev. Mod. Phys. 74:99
presets.description: Some coefficients ramp up from the vertical centre line to the left and right edges. The waves change character across the grid, from fine turbulence to broad spirals.
equations: \partial_t a = (D_a + \rho_{D} r) \nabla^2 a + \alpha a - \gamma b + (-(\beta + \rho_\beta r) a + \delta b)(a^2 + b^2)
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + \alpha b + \gamma a + (-(\beta + \rho_\beta r) b - \delta a)(a^2 + b^2)

presets.name: Guo: branching root
presets.citation: Y. Guo, M. H. Guo, J. Wu, et al. (2014) Frontiers in Plant Science; activator–inhibitor model after H. Meinhardt (1982) Models of Biological Pattern Formation
presets.description: An activator–inhibitor system with a substrate and a slow differentiation field d. From one seed a network grows and branches, and each new branch leaves a line of differentiated cells behind it.
equations: \partial_t a = C a^2 c / b - M a + s D_a \nabla^2 a + r_A d
\partial_t b = C a^2 c - N b + s D_h \nabla^2 b + r_H d
\partial_t c = C_z - G c - E_{ps}\, d c + s D_s \nabla^2 c
\partial_t d = D a - E d + \frac{d^2}{1 + F d^2}

presets.name: Erosion
presets.citation: M. Kardar, G. Parisi & Y.-C. Zhang (1986) Phys. Rev. Lett. 56:889
presets.description: A height field a erodes where it is steep, faster where the rock b is soft. Ridges and valleys sharpen out of a gentle hill. Ready uses Perlin noise for the rock; here a sum of sine waves stands in for it.
equations: \partial_t a = f \nabla^2 a - g\, |\nabla a|^{e}\, (1 + h\,(b - 1))

presets.name: Dendritic crystal
presets.citation: R. Kobayashi (1993) Physica D 63:410
presets.description: A phase-field model of a solid growing into undercooled liquid. The interface energy depends on the direction of the surface, so a small disc grows six main arms with side branches, like a snowflake.
equations: \tau\, \partial_t \phi = \nabla\cdot(\epsilon^2 \nabla \phi) - \partial_x(\epsilon \epsilon' \partial_y \phi) + \partial_y(\epsilon \epsilon' \partial_x \phi) + \phi(1 - \phi)(\phi - \tfrac12 + m)
\partial_t T = \nabla^2 T + K\, \partial_t \phi
\epsilon = \bar\epsilon\,(1 + \delta \cos(j\,(\theta + \theta_0))),\quad m = \tfrac{\alpha}{\pi} \arctan(\gamma (T_{eq} - T))
formula: var gpx = array<f32, 5>((a_e - a_w) / dx, (a_ne - a_nw) / dx, (a_e2 - a) / dx, (a_se - a_sw) / dx, (a - a_w2) / dx);
var gpy = array<f32, 5>((a_s - a_n) / dy, (a - a_n2) / dy, (a_se - a_ne) / dy, (a_s2 - a) / dy, (a_sw - a_nw) / dy);
let angle = select(atan2(gpy[i], gpx[i]), 0.0, zero) + rotate;
let grad_eps2_x = (eps[2] * eps[2] - eps[4] * eps[4]) / dx;
let grad_eps2_y = (eps[3] * eps[3] - eps[1] * eps[1]) / dy;
let m = alpha * atan(gamma * (teq - b)) / pi;
let edgp_x = (eps[4] * epsd[4] * gpy[4] - eps[2] * epsd[2] * gpy[2]) / dx;
let edgp_y = (eps[3] * epsd[3] * gpx[3] - eps[1] * epsd[1] * gpx[1]) / dy;
delta_a = (eps[0] * eps[0] * laplacian_a + edgp_x + edgp_y + grad_eps2_x * gpx[0] + grad_eps2_y * gpy[0] + a * (1.0 - a) * (a - 0.5 + m)) / tau;
presets.notes: Hand translation: Ready's formula uses C arrays and a for loop. atan2(0, 0) is made 0, as in OpenCL.

presets.name: Laplacian growth
presets.citation: R. Kobayashi (1993) Physica D 63:410
presets.description: The isotropic version of the phase-field model. A flat solid front on the left edge grows into noisy undercooled liquid and breaks into fingers that race and split.
equations: \tau\, \partial_t \phi = \bar\epsilon^2 \nabla^2 \phi + \phi(1 - \phi)(\phi - \tfrac12 + m)
\partial_t T = \nabla^2 T + K\, \partial_t \phi,\quad m = \tfrac{\alpha}{\pi} \arctan(\gamma (T_{eq} - T))

presets.name: Kuramoto–Sivashinsky chaos
presets.description: A model of flame fronts and thin falling films. Long waves grow, short waves decay, and the nonlinear term moves energy between them, so the surface forms restless cells that merge and split.

presets.name: Kuramoto–Sivashinsky cells
presets.description: The same equation on a finer grid with a smaller box. Only a few cells fit in, and the surface settles into slowly drifting cellular patterns.

presets.name: Lotka–Volterra
presets.citation: A. J. Lotka (1925) Elements of Physical Biology; V. Volterra (1926) Nature 118:558
presets.description: Prey a grow and are eaten by predators b, which die without food. With diffusion, the local boom and bust cycles fall out of step and form travelling waves of predators chasing prey.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \alpha a - \beta a b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + \delta a b - \gamma b

presets.name: Maginu parameter map
presets.citation: K. Maginu (1975) Mathematical Biosciences 27:17
presets.description: Maginu's variant of the FitzHugh–Nagumo system. α grows from left to right and γ grows along the vertical axis, so one grid shows waves, stationary patterns and uniform states side by side.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \alpha(x)\,(a - a^3) - b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + \epsilon\,(a - \gamma(y)\, b)

presets.name: Plankton patches
presets.description: Phytoplankton a, a competitor b and zooplankton c that grazes on a. From one seed in the centre, a ring of plankton spreads and breaks into irregular, drifting patches.
equations: \partial_t a = \nabla^2 a - \alpha a - e a^2 + \frac{\mu_1 a b}{1 + \omega_1 b} - \frac{a c}{1 + \gamma a}
\partial_t b = \epsilon_1 \nabla^2 b - b - b^2 + \frac{\mu_2 a b}{1 + \omega_2 a}
\partial_t c = \epsilon_2 \nabla^2 c + \frac{a c}{1 + \gamma a} - \delta c

presets.name: Plankton invasion
presets.description: Phytoplankton compete with a second species and are grazed by zooplankton. The invasion front from the centre leaves behind a patchy, chaotic mix of the three populations.
equations: \partial_t a = \nabla^2 a + a(1 - a - \chi_{12} b) - \frac{a c}{1 + \gamma a}
\partial_t b = \epsilon_1 \nabla^2 b + r b(1 - b - \chi_{21} a)
\partial_t c = \epsilon_2 \nabla^2 c + \frac{g a c}{1 + \gamma a} - \delta c

presets.name: Plankton: mortality map
presets.description: The same plankton model, but the zooplankton death rate δ grows from left to right. Regular rings on one side turn into patchy spatiotemporal chaos on the other.
equations: \partial_t a = \nabla^2 a + a(1 - a - \chi_{12} b) - \frac{a c}{1 + \gamma a}
\partial_t b = \epsilon_1 \nabla^2 b + r b(1 - b - \chi_{21} a)
\partial_t c = \epsilon_2 \nabla^2 c + \frac{g a c}{1 + \gamma a} - \delta(x)\, c

presets.name: Hexagonal spots
presets.description: The Swift–Hohenberg equation picks one wavelength. With a quadratic term β the chosen pattern is hexagons: a single bump in the centre seeds a growing lattice of spots.

presets.name: Stripes
presets.description: With β = 0 the symmetric equation prefers rolls. Stripes spread from the central bump and from the noise, and then slowly anneal their defects.

presets.name: Phyllotaxis hexagons
presets.description: Pennybacker and Newell's plant-growth model adds a gradient term that makes hexagons robust. From one bump, a hexagonal lattice of primordia, like the florets of a sunflower, spreads out.
equations:
\partial_t a = \mu a - (1 + 
abla^2)^2 a -  eta\,(|
abla a|^2 + 2 a 
abla^2 a) - a^3

presets.name: Phyllotaxis ring
presets.description: The plant-growth model seeded with a ring of bumps near the edge, like the rim of a growing shoot. New bumps fill in between the old ones and pack inward.
equations:
\partial_t a = \mu a - (1 + 
abla^2)^2 a -  eta\,(|
abla a|^2 + 2 a 
abla^2 a) - a^3

presets.name: Swift–Hohenberg parameter map
presets.description: μ grows from left to right and β grows along the vertical axis. The grid shows the uniform state, stripes, hexagonal spots and inverted spots, with smooth changes between them.
equations: \partial_t a = \mu(x)\, a - (1 + \nabla^2)^2 a + \beta(y)\, a^2 - a^3

presets.name: Dissipative solitons
presets.citation: C. P. Schenk, M. Or-Guil, M. Bode & H.-G. Purwins (1997) Phys. Rev. Lett. 78:3781
presets.description: A three-component model of gas-discharge spots. Seven offset pairs of blobs turn into particle-like spots that move, collide, scatter and sometimes merge.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \lambda a - a^3 - k_3 c - b + k_1
\tau\, \partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a - b
\theta\, \partial_t c = D_c \nabla^2 c + a - c

presets.name: Soliton molecules
presets.citation: C. P. Schenk, M. Or-Guil, M. Bode & H.-G. Purwins (1997) Phys. Rev. Lett. 78:3781
presets.description: The gas-discharge model with other constants. The moving spots bind together into small groups that travel as one, like molecules made of solitons.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \lambda a - a^3 - k_3 c - b + k_1
\tau\, \partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a - b
\theta\, \partial_t c = D_c \nabla^2 c + a - c

presets.name: Predator–prey spirals
presets.description: Prey grow to a carrying capacity and predators have a saturating appetite. The local cycles are stable limit cycles, and with diffusion they form spiral waves and patchy chaos.

presets.name: Predator–prey map (h, k)
presets.description: The half-saturation h grows from left to right and the conversion rate k grows along the vertical axis. Steady coexistence, waves and turbulence share one grid.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + a(1 - a) - \frac{a}{a + h(x)}\, b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + k(y) \frac{a}{a + h(x)}\, b - m b

presets.name: Predator–prey map (h, m)
presets.description: The half-saturation h grows from left to right and the predator death rate m grows along the vertical axis. Where m is high the predators die out and the grid goes flat.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + a(1 - a) - \frac{a}{a + h(x)}\, b
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + k \frac{a}{a + h(x)}\, b - m(y)\, b

presets.name: Schlögl domains
presets.citation: F. Schlögl (1972) Z. Physik 253:147
presets.description: A single chemical with two stable states, +1 and −1. Tiny noise decides which state wins at each place, and the domains then coarsen as curved walls shrink.
equations: \partial_t a = \nabla^2 a + a - a^3

presets.name: Two-slit interference
presets.citation: E. Schrödinger (1926) Phys. Rev. 28:1049
presets.description: A quantum wave packet, written as its real part a and imaginary part b, moves right toward a wall with two slits. The view shows the probability |ψ|² (plus the wall), with the familiar interference fringes behind the wall.
equations: \partial_t a = -\nabla^2 b - V b
\partial_t b = \nabla^2 a + V a

presets.name: Wave packet on a barrier
presets.citation: E. Schrödinger (1926) Phys. Rev. 28:1049
presets.description: A Gaussian wave packet hits a potential step. Part of it reflects and part of it tunnels through, and the two parts interfere where they overlap.
equations: \partial_t a = -\nabla^2 b - V b
\partial_t b = \nabla^2 a + V a

presets.name: Turing's spots
presets.description: The model from Turing's 1952 paper on morphogenesis, the first reaction–diffusion account of biological pattern. A random start separates into regular dappled spots.

presets.name: Turing's spots with noise
presets.description: Turing's model started from a flat state, with a noise field c that keeps disturbing b. The noise alone is enough to seed the spots.
equations: \partial_t a = k\,(16 - a b) + D_a \nabla^2 a
\partial_t b = \max\big(-b,\; k\,(a b - b - 12) + 2\xi + D_b \nabla^2 b\big)
\xi \leftarrow (\xi + \nabla^2 \xi) \bmod 1

presets.name: Turing parameter map
presets.description: The reaction rate k grows from left to right and the inhibitor diffusion D_b grows along the vertical axis. Spot size and spacing change smoothly across the grid.
equations: \partial_t a = k(x)\,(16 - a b) + D_a \nabla^2 a
\partial_t b = \max\big(-b,\; k(x)\,(a b - b - 12) + D_b(y)\, \nabla^2 b\big)

presets.name: Yang: target waves
presets.description: Two Brusselator layers, each with its own diffusion rates, coupled cell by cell. One layer makes Turing spots and the other makes waves, and the mix gives patterns that neither layer makes alone.

presets.name: Yang: oscillating spots
presets.description: With weak coupling, the Turing layer forms spots that blink on and off in step with the oscillating layer.

presets.name: Yang: black-eye
presets.description: Two Turing modes with different wavelengths interact. Large hexagons carry smaller spots in their centres, the so-called black-eye pattern.

presets.name: Yang: superlattice
presets.description: Two spatial modes lock into a superlattice: a regular array of large and small spots with a longer repeat than either mode alone.

presets.name: Yang: twinkling eyes
presets.description: A Turing lattice whose spots oscillate out of phase with their neighbours, so the pattern seems to twinkle.

presets.name: Kyttä: labyrinth
presets.description: Kyttä's version of the coupled Brusselators uses a cubic coupling. With these rates the layers settle into a labyrinth of stripes.

presets.name: Kyttä: spots in spots
presets.description: Weak cubic coupling between two Turing layers with very different wavelengths. Fine spots of one layer sit on the coarse pattern of the other.

presets.name: Kyttä: strong coupling
presets.description: The same layers with stronger coupling. The two wavelengths lock together and the result is a more regular, mixed pattern.

presets.name: Oregonator spirals
presets.citation: R. J. Field & R. M. Noyes (1974) J. Chem. Phys. 60:1877; J. J. Tyson & P. C. Fife (1980) J. Chem. Phys. 73:2224
presets.description: The two-variable Oregonator, a model of the Belousov–Zhabotinsky reaction. Two broken wave segments curl up at their free ends into a pair of counter-rotating spirals.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a \nabla^2 a + \frac{1}{\epsilon}\Big(a - a^2 - f b\, \frac{a - q}{a + q}\Big)
\partial_t b = D_b \nabla^2 b + a - b

presets.name: Heat equation
presets.description: Two noisy hot blocks cool by pure diffusion. The noise vanishes first, then the blocks blur into smooth blobs, and the box relaxes toward one uniform temperature.
equations: \partial_t a = \nabla^2 a

presets.name: Laplace interpolation
presets.description: Diffusion runs only where the mask b is zero, and the masked shapes keep their values. The field relaxes to the harmonic function that fills the gaps between them.
equations: \partial_t a = [\,b = 0\,]\; \nabla^2 a

presets.name: Biharmonic interpolation
presets.citation: Biharmonic (thin-plate) interpolation; stencil from M. Patra & M. Karttunen (2006) Numer. Methods PDE 22:936
presets.description: The same fill-in problem with the bi-Laplacian. The result is the smooth surface of a thin plate pinned to the shapes, with gentle overshoot between them.
equations: \partial_t a = -[\,b = 0\,]\; \nabla^4 a

presets.name: Wave equation
presets.citation: J. le Rond d'Alembert (1747) Hist. Acad. R. Sci. Berlin 3:214
presets.description: A bump released at rest spreads as a circular wave that reflects from the walls. The second field b holds the velocity; the step updates b first and then a, which keeps the scheme stable.
equations: \partial_t b = \nabla^2 a
\partial_t a = b

presets.name: Shallow water
presets.citation: A. J. C. de Saint-Venant (1871) C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 73:147
presets.description: Linearised shallow-water flow in a basin with a wall along the edges and a breakwater in the middle. A mound of water collapses and its waves reflect and diffract around the barrier.
equations: \partial_t h = -\max(0, h - z)\,(\partial_x u + \partial_y v)
\partial_t u = -g\, \partial_x h - k u
\partial_t v = -g\, \partial_y h - k v

presets.name: Splats
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Cornus Ammonis
presets.description: Two Swift–Hohenberg-like fields, each smoothed by a Gaussian blur and weakly coupled to the other. They separate into round splats that jostle and slowly lock into place.
equations: \partial_t a = g_a G*a + w_4 \nabla^4 a + w_2 \nabla^2 a + s a - a^3 + D_b b
\partial_t b = g_b G*b + w_4' \nabla^4 b + w_2' \nabla^2 b + s b - b^3 + D_a a

presets.name: Rock–paper–scissors
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Tiha von Ghyczy; cyclic competition as in T. Reichenbach, M. Mobilia & E. Frey (2007) Nature 448:1046
presets.description: Three species in cyclic dominance: a beats b, b beats c, c beats a. None can win for good, so the populations chase each other in rotating spirals.
equations: \partial_t a = k \nabla^2 a + g a(1 - a) + m(a b - c a)
\partial_t b = k \nabla^2 b + g b(1 - b) + m(b c - a b)
\partial_t c = k \nabla^2 c + g c(1 - c) + m(c a - b c)

presets.name: Sobel waves
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Tiha von Ghyczy
presets.description: Diffusion plus a Sobel edge filter that points to the south-west. The filter acts like advection with a grain, and the noise flows into diagonal wave trains.
equations: \partial_t a = k_1 \nabla^2 a + k_2\, S_{SW} * a

presets.name: Surfing solitons
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Cornus Ammonis
presets.description: The complex worms rule with a Sobel edge coupling and a local-sum field. Compact blobs form and ride the wave fronts like surfers.
equations: \partial_t a = D_a (a^2 - b^2) + s_a \nabla^2 b + c_a b - \kappa_a\, \mathrm{sgn}(a) a^2

\partial_t b = d_s |
abla_S a \cdot 
abla_S b|_{\mathbb C} + D_b a b - s_b 
abla^2 a + c_b a - \kappa_b\, \mathrm{sgn}(b) b^2

presets.name: Orbits
presets.citation: Ready community pattern by Dan Wills
presets.description: Each cell iterates a complex power map, as in fractal orbit art, and the pair (a, b) diffuses and cross-diffuses. The result is sharp, fast-moving wave fronts.
equations: z = a + i b,\quad w = z + z_0
\partial_t z = \mathrm{clamp}\big(\Delta t\, w^{p} + D \nabla^2 z + z_c\big)
